nova-3:621a7e7bf68b047500d2afaeb51876a6b.transcript: His evidence in 1814, said it was more.

nova-3:891ff2df780ac485d634173a55c223921.transcript: And gave the garnish for the common side at that sum, which is 5 shillings more than mister Neild says was extorted on the common side.

nova-3:a39ccca550d83bac40d888950d0af2612.transcript: Numerous tyrannies were practiced on all who would not and could not pay the garnish.

nova-3:8a1c016ee5236809ff2cd88ab89ab5397.transcript: And so we're unable either to warm themselves or to cook their food.

nova-3:3455f76636512f125f33dbb525d5c8260.transcript: They were made to wash and swab the ward, or they were shut out from the ward fireplace and forbidden to pass a chalked line drawn on the floor.

nova-3:5e1fe21f9804987bcd039444e1ec2475f.transcript: Besides these fees, legitimate and illegitimate, there were others which must be paid before release.

nova-3:6b753af5d1e37da96751dc7268e7495c7.transcript: The sheriff demanded 4 shillings, 6p for his liberate, the jailer 6 shillings, 10p more, and the turnkey 2 shillings.

nova-3:a2e3e8c78e09378009eb361fc2354139f.transcript: And thus, when the debtor's debt had been actually paid or when he had abandoned his property to the creditors and almost destitute

nova-3:2f7c8c7717f86d76950af844124d281b7.transcript: Looked forward to his liberty. He was still delayed until he had paid a new debt arising, quote

nova-3:45abd7b42f4458ea4138644cc89fbe8c9.transcript: Nor was nonpayment made a pretext for further imprisonment, thanks to the humanity of the jailer or the funds provided by various charities.

nova-3:a8a7aba9863ae4a272125f3f306e41bd1.transcript: Only out of a satisfaction of all his former debts, end quote. The fees were not always extorted. It is true.

nova-3:86e0d8f08a976c58459dabd320c121eff.transcript: There was this much honest forbearance in Newgate in these days.

nova-3:67d0e30139937ebdbceffa18953923d4d.transcript: The debtors who could afford the cabin and master's side were not permitted to share in the prison charities.

nova-3:42bd380f1b3c08e6eae63fe99f273f688.transcript: These were lumped together into a general fund.

nova-3:b09a266fdafc49de44784fe218da01d8a.transcript: And a calculation made as to the amount that might be expended per week from the whole sum so that the latter might last out the year.

nova-3:5eb180bbb5c836141a7603aada7d381ff.transcript: It generally ran to about £6 per week. The money, which at one time had been distributed quarterly and all went in drink

nova-3:f219c9abf1a51ae531a693d87c7b73c9b.transcript: Was after eighteen o seven through the exertions of the keeper of the jail spent in the purchase of necessaries.

nova-3:d394f8a8be3924589484fdfa476bdd48e.transcript: But this weekly pittance did not go far when the debtor's side was crowded as it often was.

nova-3:ed3cd0a9fc9848547985d18b7e90263ba.transcript: Notably as when numbers filled Newgate in anticipation of Lord Redisdale's bill for insolvent debtors.

nova-3:f3097fc754d597c261d9f4e52a4538346.transcript: And there were as many as 350 prisoners in at one time.

nova-3:eb555717e03542490e89a1347ae2dcef6.transcript: The city also allowed the poor debtors 14 ounces of bread daily and their share of eight stone of meat, an allowance which never varied.

nova-3:cbff5e77a419c39e0db589792aadd7f0b.transcript: Issued once a week and divided as far as it would go. A very precarious and uncertain ration.

nova-3:1d1d86bd017c6c3287ea395e7b96f91d2.transcript: The bread was issued every alternate day. And while some prisoners often ate their whole allowance at once

nova-3:d91b6440609e9342eafe67afbc614b655.transcript: The keeper made them a special grant of 6p per diem out of the common stock.

nova-3:a353a29d434f595b0ddb273ef03703442.transcript: Or the 6p allowance was claimed for the creditors, which seldom happened owing to the expense the process entailed.

nova-3:468f9dbfb4673f94c5700ae371edba725.transcript: Hence, starvation stared many in the face unless friends from outside came to their assistance.

nova-3:24e93952c15b894f1cabe12a03926e3a8.transcript: The poor debtors were not supplied with beds. Those who could pay the price might hire them from each other.

nova-3:e725e4031bf2e8bc7c4f2e0349c9a1ea6.transcript: Share in the weekly allowance of meat might also be denied to debtors who had not paid garnish as well as in the weekly grant from the charitable fund.

nova-3:71e484dd1546168551940456b943eaf1a.transcript: Others who arrived just after the time of distribution were often forty eight hours without food. The latter might also be six days without meat.

nova-3:633b5ed75771ffec5a7f89710e3dc9ea6.transcript: Or from persons who made a trade of it, or they might bring their beds with them into the prison.

nova-3:587f5c04d2ce8b39292128eb1833b9465.transcript: Failing any of these methods, seeing that Strah was forbidden for fear of fire, they had to be satisfied with a couple of the rugs provided by the city.

nova-3:448bbb89fab276ec55ae2a95c62c53304.transcript: The supply of which was, however, limited, and there were not always enough to give bedding to all. The stock was diminished by theft.

nova-3:fa028c8b4613f5193c75a64d95f7f64bc.transcript: Female visitors carried them out of the prisons, or the debtors destroyed them when the weather was warm.

nova-3:24798c7e3ce9d33b7b3d9743d2a8745d6.transcript: And they were not in great demand in order to convert them into mop heads or cleaning rags.

nova-3:c9d5cc72227212a49b1c0d50d72e4f870.transcript: Sometimes rugs were urgently required and not forthcoming.

nova-3:f7d3b632ca77a089c6b63b4837f0a18ee.transcript: A severe winter set in. The new stock had not been supplied by the contractors, and the poor debtors perished of cold.

nova-3:936432a37902fa036af7ab8392196c46a.transcript: Again, there was no regular allowance of fuel. Coals were purchased out of the garnish money and the charitable fund.

nova-3:7353fdd703e26ebf1f3f28d0c2ba01c81.transcript: Indeed, the place with its oak floors cocked with pitch and smoked ceilings

nova-3:65c0eb3916cc0939316eaca2dfad4e139.transcript: So were candles, salt, pepper, mops, and brooms, but the latter could have been of little service. Dirt prevailed everywhere.

nova-3:1d955e879cf59990b23111e00fdad3c4b.transcript: Only now and again, in extreme cases, an unusually nasty companion was stripped, hailed to the pump.

nova-3:b9802584786ba6f1b1b0b4998c3e60be0.transcript: Could not be made even to look clean while there was no obligation of personal cleanliness on individuals who often came into the prison in filthy rags.

nova-3:abd363130b92b9c6a2bb9eac2f8030bae.transcript: The Chronicles of Newgate volume two by Arthur Griffiths. Section five, Newgate down to 18 '18 part two.

nova-3:42e6d22eacee598c737ccc8e6c27d1d30.transcript: The squalor and uncleanness of the debtor's side was intensified by constant overcrowding.

nova-3:a14150d91e410ec0a9c48fa77cadb0adc.transcript: Prisoners were committed to it quite without reference to its capacity.

nova-3:9996587667150a605e82968efc68850ad.transcript: Besides this, although the families of debtors were no longer permitted to live with them inside the jail

nova-3:a1344ca7fc6bb53b75e864ae2dc6993d3.transcript: No steps taken to reduce the number of committals, and the governor was obliged to utilize the chapel as a day and night room.

nova-3:8b768ffc1c709ac5e33fedc38290636de.transcript: Hundreds of women and children came in every morning to spend the day there, and there was no limitation whatever to the numbers of visitors admitted to the debtor's side.

nova-3:61db8b94c77a8f64e2b06d0f1ccee0938.transcript: Friends arrived about 9AM and went out at 9PM when as many as 200 visitors have been observed leaving the debtors' yards at one time.

nova-3:bb3ae9fdab3bd4f9d639de0490ec6fce9.transcript: The day passed in revelry and drunkenness. Although spirituous liquors were forbidden

nova-3:a2e6c36464f3d78a24986da6dfc9e514c.transcript: Wine and beer might be had in any quantity, the only limitation being

nova-3:a9e6e40e5ebbead10c469464e9c769450.transcript: And debtors might practically have as much as they liked if they could only pay for it.

nova-3:bdaf813e646599e9c935344820afbb1c9.transcript: That not more than one bottle of wine or one quart of beer could be issued at one time. No account was taken of the amount of liquors admitted in one day.

nova-3:a5a1db3ab443e4a2b99658a295caafb51.transcript: No attempt was made to check drunkenness beyond the penalty of shutting out friends from any ward in which a prisoner exceeded.

nova-3:46819996587503bbc2fa7e774805cccfb.transcript: Quarreling among the debtors was not infrequent. Blows were struck, and fights often ensued.

nova-3:f9ab4ca474818774b51a56f947fb322bd.transcript: For this and other acts of misconduct, there was the discipline of the refractory ward or strong room on the debtor's side.

nova-3:940ebfd2975d08ecfa4765082b716d7ef.transcript: Bad cases were removed to a cell on the felon's side, and here they were locked in solitary confinement for three days at a time.

nova-3:78bdbcbbd94b60c7c58aa2b732d984e8c.transcript: Order throughout the debtor's side was preserved.

nova-3:d32813f18db3d60789da0f8bd34e98efd.transcript: And discipline maintained by a system open to grave abuses and which had the prescription of long usage.

nova-3:cd668a35890e1eca1f165e6ae3bfcdfee.transcript: And which was never wholly rooted out for many years to come.

nova-3:b3394b43923f796a33331f57c6ccdbd9c.transcript: This was the pernicious plan of governing by prisoners or of setting a favored few in authority over the many.

nova-3:d338280da5f298d0436eff0317fa7a1ce.transcript: The head of the debtors' prison was a prisoner called the steward who was chosen by the whole body from six whom the keeper nominated.

nova-3:17c10ada2c3d13121d862ac6ed6b9e74d.transcript: All the allowances of food passed through his hands. He had the control of the pour box for chance charities.

nova-3:a3ddf9981b079be96f85f2e07b593bb65.transcript: Collected the garnish money and distributed the weekly grant from the prison charitable fund.

nova-3:983d2eae47cd408ca4f476dc7740ba5c9.transcript: In the latter duties, he was, however, supervised by three auditors, freely chosen by the prisoners among themselves.

nova-3:35a9bb1a63a1bcb3092325c11acac8c38.transcript: The auditors were paid a shilling each for their services each time the pour box was opened. The steward was also remunerated for his trouble.

nova-3:cbc8e88ee2895af66042be8eaba4cdcc7.transcript: And no doubt made the meat also pay toll.

nova-3:f12c1b55431559f3730a699c284ae18dd.transcript: He had a double allowance of bread deducted, of course, from the already too limited portion of the rest.

nova-3:02cba6284a962c94b8db75a8bb3f317d4.transcript: Under the steward, there were captains of wards chosen in the same way and performing analogous duties.

nova-3:24ba3760e8b16219b6540a53aa32b74ec.transcript: These subordinate chiefs were also rewarded out of the scanty prison rations.

nova-3:6320bf10d847d12ab34334859089ae123.transcript: So valuable were they deemed that as much as 50 guineas was offered to the keeper for the post.

nova-3:e289466d7c52c8fd21ee9d4e549446b8f.transcript: The same system was extended to the criminal side, and cases were on record of the place of wardsman being sold for considerable sums.

nova-3:662511021f14e331493f890439862a535.transcript: This gradually was forced upon the consciousness of the corporation.

nova-3:58bf633a1de535ab6baae6c9fafc8e6d4.transcript: Enough has been said probably to prove that there was room for improvement in the condition and treatment of debtors in the prisons of the city of London.

nova-3:78ee0254e35e909ced4bb3498635f7289.transcript: And about 1812 application was made to parliament for funds to build a new debtors' prison.

nova-3:5854be3ae11813849dda19ace7a26d8e6.transcript: Authority was given to raise money on the orphans fund to the extent of £90,000.

nova-3:7a5d8006879a6add7e725ba326401d67f.transcript: Which would accommodate the inmates of Newgate and of the three copters, Ludgate.

nova-3:c25209f5630305cccc253ac54ef0c499b.transcript: Site was purchased between Red Line And White Cross Streets and a new prison planned.

nova-3:226fe8fb6261a75d8f4b4d3508f8e58a4.transcript: Guiltspur Street and the poultry or about 476 in all.

nova-3:bf1d3dd9c03376ff0c83225e29fb9a93c.transcript: The evils of association for these debtors were perpetuated, although the plan provided for the separation of the various contingents committed to it.

nova-3:ca9d4ac11636cb1b218a23c1a9f889910.transcript: There was no lack of air and light for the new jail and several exercising yards.

nova-3:fa6c1d02212cba71a8b85f25cccb08386.transcript: The completion of this very necessary building was, however, much delayed for want of funds.

nova-3:e986a39adeeb2b5303d7ef2782825d765.transcript: And it was not ready to relieve Newgate till late in 1815.

nova-3:25321ab3000231eaa5f97cc4288436581.transcript: Reforms which were to be attempted in that prison.

nova-3:06738a60d2fe101352ad5f007e09a7e6f.transcript: More particularly as regarded the classification of prisoners and which were dependent on the space to be gained by the removal of the debtors.

nova-3:71e964557fc84f5dfcdf6804f3678c51a.transcript: Could not be carried out till then. It is to be feared that long after the opening of White Cross Street Prison

nova-3:2ef5c97c5d8eed082fd0eeb4482f3172f.transcript: Newgate continued to be a reproach to those responsible for its management.

nova-3:ce6a6d070a807a95dc186717152b275ea.transcript: I pass now to the criminal side of Newgate, which consisted of the six quarters or yards already enumerated and described.

nova-3:0fc4f7ff70b0b8f460fdf78b353550208.transcript: The inmates of this part, as distinguished from the debtors, were comprised in four classes.

nova-3:4536ce1f38b00176b53c0bab7cf010ec2.transcript: Two persons under sentence of imprisonment for a fixed period or until they shall have paid certain fines.

nova-3:f880f059c6f6508dead3c7e363cc65c7b.transcript: Three, transports awaiting removal to the colonies, and four, capital convicts condemned to death and awaiting execution.

nova-3:38303397a7bbf801f5d53480f51bb8e9c.transcript: At one time, the whole of these different categories were thrown together pell mell young and old, the untried with the convicted.

nova-3:6f019cca816f4733a6aea523438dcadae.transcript: Imperfect attempt at classification was, however, made in 1812, and a yard was as far as possible set apart for the untried.

nova-3:a2238a9a130661ea0a8aea63f27a2d233.transcript: Or class one, with whom under the imperious demand for accommodation were also associated the misdemeanors, or class two.

nova-3:77e9fa217782224bda996103235ddb44e.transcript: This was the chapel yard with its five wards, which were calculated to hold 70 prisoners but often held many more.

nova-3:9faa16941dc8d9d00b70658ddac5ce3e3.transcript: A further subclassification was attempted by separating at night those charged with misdemeanors from those charged with felony.

nova-3:1b866dd83fa2b7b4dcb943831adfff722.transcript: But all mingled freely during the day in the yard.

nova-3:938c5d7eaefabf8c467cdc5a7834a1919.transcript: Which was a wooden flooring on a slightly inclined plane with a beam running across the top to serve as a pillow.

nova-3:2e3ec5e23757947a19f26d793648c440f.transcript: Sleeping accommodation in the Chapel yard wards, and indeed throughout the prison, consisted of a barrack bed.

nova-3:0dba21998fac83a755ada9f79b9bdfe9e.transcript: No beds were issued. Only two rugs per prisoner.

nova-3:bf21ae6862dcff29652352e1cd605a376.transcript: When each sleeper had the full lateral space allotted to him, it amounted to one foot and a half on the barrack bed.

nova-3:60ea79177c0cedd67a58b93f3d9605857.transcript: But when the ward was obliged to accommodate double the ordinary number, as was frequently the case

nova-3:b33cf72711901c0bdf361505f9225f79c.transcript: The sleepers covered the entire floor with the exception of a passage in the middle.

nova-3:fb4ce04f2a78645c21593bd8ed0528716.transcript: All the misdemeanants, whatever their offense, were lodged in this Chapel Ward.

nova-3:7c3050d653790dda1eea2e00e7a7e55c1.transcript: As many various and according to our ideas, heinous crimes came under this head.

nova-3:2f291d44ac66e533c0dccaea0c3dcafa1.transcript: The then existing state of the law,

nova-3:fa5a6be152006ac42357685ef3070cc73.transcript: The man guilty of a common assault found himself side by side with the fraudulent or others who had attempted abominable crimes.

nova-3:7daedfcc6ef8aa22c6878aaa67a4b74aa.transcript: In this heterogeneous society, we're also thrown the unfortunate journalists to whom I have already referred and on whom imprisonment in Newgate

nova-3:0072f438751a3c0ad9e802023d83ee897.transcript: Was frequently adjudged for so called libels or too outspoken comments in print.

nova-3:6ed526229b8ff0875e674fbaa8acb91de.transcript: Was particularly recommended by the committee on jails in 1814.

nova-3:6647de9fdbe8fe8285e956b74408c6ada.transcript: That some other and less mixed prison should be used for the confinement of persons convicted of libels, but this suggestion was ignored.

nova-3:43b953ccf7f0ea2843abb06ea688ee7bb.transcript: Indeed, the partial classification attempted seems to have been abandoned within a year or two.

nova-3:392e5263fa372a9818727f9b233822056.transcript: The honorable H. G. Bennett, who visited Newgate in 1817, saw in one yard and a total of 72 prisoners.

nova-3:e9c39b9463056ed3ff6b37d3906c84ccb.transcript: 35 tried and 37 untried. Of the former, three were transports for life.

nova-3:a4531ada24337935c9ed86262d25184e5.transcript: Four for fourteen years, and three of them persons sentenced to fines or short imprisonment, one for little more than a month.

nova-3:61efb21b80544833fa3262f2789088d85.transcript: Two of the untried were for murder and several for housebreaking and highway robbery.

nova-3:38443cc94e1699f5809437baae2fcf408.transcript: Nor were the misdemeanants and bail prisoners any longer separated from those whose crimes were of a more serious character.

nova-3:d099166c2843c1fb94fc9bd8123b94c57.transcript: Mister Bennett refers to a gentleman confined for want of bail who occupied a room with five others.

nova-3:be33843de1e387ab49cd5148af24399f0.transcript: Two committed by the bankruptcy commissioner, one for perjury and two transports.

nova-3:244713775e9eb2df7e5f0dbedd8fdaac5.transcript: Persons convicted of publishing libels were still immured in the same rooms with transports and felons.

nova-3:a15d4297b1a202e48104dc2ce2139f11c.transcript: The middle yard, as far as its limits would permit, was appropriated to felons and transports. The wards here were generally very crowded.

nova-3:2aeba6074d4d0ee7ddb227b6a983e8086.transcript: Each ward was calculated to hold 24, allowing each individual one foot and a half.

nova-3:0b9e7b41d5df8ec1f387f25bc9763ef8f.transcript: These 24 could just sleep on the barrack bed. When the number was higher and it often rose to 40, the surplus had to sleep on the floor.

nova-3:a273967f8d4c9b6ced3302d2ad97f5f53.transcript: Quote, a common sized man, says the keeper, mister Newman, can turn in 19 inches, end quote.

nova-3:11d9c0413f167aa5858d72e39ece5a9fe.transcript: The crowding was in consequence of the delay in removing transports.

nova-3:21344891e6cbf70186f1c959bd383c0e5.transcript: These often remained in Newgate for six months, sometimes a year, in some cases longer.

nova-3:c943f72b2a97287c0cfe3a940ae203044.transcript: Occasionally, the transports made themselves so useful in the jail that they were passed over.

nova-3:1952e50d7da3ee1b3f0e0261e976910b2.transcript: In one, for seven years, that of a man sentenced to death for whom great interest had been made, but whom it was not thought right to pardon.

nova-3:d015f29716549ee913a05ad07c84a2445.transcript: Mister Newman admitted that he had petitioned that certain trusty men might be left in the jail.

nova-3:4e6e9a0b9dc74f90efe21e1f41498e648.transcript: Constantly associated with these convicted felons were numbers of juveniles, infants of tender years.

nova-3:6b3b6e6ed35ad835876e85949bc1dcf45.transcript: There were frequently in the middle yard seven or eight children, the youngest barely nine.

nova-3:0b180de7afa9e2cb9139aee83fa3b9aa6.transcript: The oldest, only 12 or 13, exposed to all the contaminating influences of the place.

nova-3:64d6d6af892f2a84cc52290204d7ea367.transcript: Mister Bennett mentions also the case of young men of better stamp, clerks in city offices, and youths of good parentage.

nova-3:9b5e9e38f07f979fb0b2ae85aa7f3db93.transcript: Quote, in this dreadful situation, end quote, who had been rescued from the Hulks through the kindness and attention of the secretary of state

nova-3:6de0dbb23be38932b5e0b5f01b86304b4.transcript: Quote, yet they had been long enough, he goes on to say, in the prison associated with the lowest and vilest criminals.

nova-3:a99ea16fed2007cfa88a95a119c61efaf.transcript: With convicts of all ages and characters to render it next to impossible, but that with the obliteration of all sense of self respect.

nova-3:56ffb9d5e23307926ec7bc24d5da1bbea.transcript: The inevitable consequence of such a situation, their morals must have been destroyed.

nova-3:a6f565e5828508d0dd8e8867d824a7aaa.transcript: And though distress or the seduction of others might have led to the commission of this, their first offense

nova-3:d9c0524cb49ba9459c07192d4671572af.transcript: Yet the society they were driven to live in, the language they daily heard, and the lessons they were taught in this academy.

nova-3:689a243787cec75a501652582ba6497ce.transcript: Must have had a tendency to turn them into the world hardened and accomplished in the ways of vice and crime, end quote.

nova-3:0b917cc1f975960ce1ad7c262678badc9.transcript: Mister Buxton, in the work already quoted, instances another grievous case of the horrors of indiscriminate association in Newgate.

nova-3:e235d6933f16af4faefd24a7d896bac62.transcript: Was that of a person, quote, who practiced in the law and who was connected by marriage with some very respectable families.

nova-3:176978ede224eb05aec12363f5e2373cb.transcript: Was sent on to Newgate in a coach, handcuffed to a noted housebreaker, who was afterwards cast for death.

nova-3:7bb93c2f520b74965956abfdd289ba05f.transcript: The first night in Newgate and for the subsequent fortnight.

nova-3:3240d963ca05b7dd38385644dbcbbef6b.transcript: Spirits were freely introduced, and although he had first abstained,

nova-3:2601c2ab52edf86284ef16673c1886907.transcript: Slept in the same bed with a highwayman on one side and a man charged with murder on the other.

nova-3:21a09a8c6ddbc3a49da5b2762efb6968f.transcript: They viewed him with some suspicion as one of whom they knew nothing.

nova-3:ffc2c61da066ca2962165620d44588468.transcript: Found he must adopt the manners of his companions or that his life would be in danger.

nova-3:a7583b8707f80cb885bddbd3ee3577e18.transcript: When any prisoner committed an offense against the community or against an individual, he was tried by a court in the jail.

nova-3:3c1e99074d633a0760ddd68a45d903359.transcript: He was in consequence put out of the protection of their internal law, end quote. Their code was a subject of some curiosity.

nova-3:81e021b906f5c429dc9905576f183333d.transcript: A prisoner, generally the oldest and most dextrous thief.

nova-3:2ef1808fc1b7ccca0f5bae68bd5239c8f.transcript: Was appointed judge, and a towel tied in knots was hung on each side in imitation of a wig.

nova-3:2d22f064adbb6b4ddc8b5eef7b2d01e3f.transcript: The judge sat in proper form. He was punctiliously styled, my lord.

nova-3:3225166f02190b435fc50469e163d1adc.transcript: A jury having been selected and duly sworn, the culprit was then arraigned. Justice, however, was not administered with absolute integrity.

nova-3:613c05cb4e85f0bfb6653ae7d01ee0e20.transcript: A bribe to the judge was certain to secure acquittal, and the neglect of the formality was certainly followed by condemnation.

nova-3:4dc435f7f06bef385abf13e91fca20c25.transcript: Various punishments were inflicted, the heaviest of which was standing in the pillory.

nova-3:3c98e531510c1e74830ea09166f605019.transcript: After a few years of active exertion, the society was rewarded by fresh legislation.

nova-3:42696700c5d40dc404f710f6197cec2a6.transcript: To its efforts and their effect upon parliament and the public mind, we must attribute the new jail acts of four George the fourth.

nova-3:0abcdddeb2fc43f5a60347a8449772c05.transcript: By the preamble of the first named act, it was declared

nova-3:428c209d620f38e633a073ff0b9bbcf98.transcript: Accordingly, due provision was made for the enforcement of hard labor on all prisoners sentenced to it and for the employment of all others.

nova-3:de68b40a45864b3e6494192ef770a69fb.transcript: It was plain that although the law had defined general principles of prison government

nova-3:8ca3ad78fc2c7e6bf29af41c1ef5ba7c9.transcript: When the new acts were introduced, numerous prisons under local jurisdiction were exempted from the operation of the law.

nova-3:be86252a6227300548bdda90b8cf41db2.transcript: The great architectural experiment, which grew out of the strong representations of Jeremy Bentham and others, and was the first national recognition of the principle

nova-3:de98282df6977630eaa022a478af87ed8.transcript: Messrs. Crawford and Russell proceeded to carry out their new functions with commendable energy and without a moment's loss of time.

nova-3:bdb2cdf286ee2002eae1a94712afd2889.transcript: The ink was barely dry upon their letters of appointment before they appeared at Newgate and commenced a searching investigation.

nova-3:e788bc7addc924f2612ea4e7de9a95285.transcript: They attended early and late. They mustered the prisoners, examined into their condition.

nova-3:da6195de4ed4a22cda594cb42a87528db.transcript: Took voluminous evidence from all classes of individuals, from the governor down to the convict in the condemned cells.

nova-3:e0be074f73ae27ebfb7870b8a74fdd5c2.transcript: They visited the wards after locking up time and saw with their own eyes what went on.

nova-3:0ae8452bcf2f89cbb04744e561b0e7811.transcript: A subject of magnitude and importance sufficient to exclude other jails. They soon narrowed their inquiry still further.

nova-3:851a872a3a6dfc2a70684678a85707048.transcript: And limited it to Newgate alone. Newgate indeed became the sole theme of their first report.

nova-3:0f50ca655b4f7844aa67b6c08bab84e39.transcript: The fact was that the years as they passed, nearly twenty in all, had worked but little permanent improvement in this detestable prison.

nova-3:11ca81c9479ca5f4f3e802c55e0ac4162.transcript: Changes introduced under pressure had been only skin deep.

nova-3:841d221eb97e26655aa4633550a9a6a79.transcript: Relapse was rapid and inevitable so that the latter state of the prison was worse than the first.

nova-3:88ae4aa4d9d345ffc4ddc8002a9720b0d.transcript: The disgraceful overcrowding had been partially ended, but the same evils of indiscriminate association were still present. There was the old neglect of decency.

nova-3:f6425bc6b0f85728894a03cc4123122bc.transcript: The same callous indifference to the moral well-being of the prisoners, the same one of employment and of all disciplinary control.

nova-3:e91bfd70526ec6d018f552da9e0b5602b.transcript: All these evils were set forth at length in the inspector's first report.

nova-3:f5a3f3fa52704aa6d9ff1973634c0077e.transcript: There was no longer the faintest possible excuse for overcrowding. The numbers now committed to Newgate had sensibly diminished.

nova-3:e99f0691f3402420b0f6352222d19b2ce.transcript: The prison had become more or less a place of detention only, harboring mainly those awaiting trial.

nova-3:cb36d1e4df14ec9a503757c6163b09041.transcript: To these were still added an average of about 50 expecting the last penalty of the law, a certain number of transports awaiting removal to the colonies.

nova-3:2d6dc560298549bbfe6bc81d4437ee9b2.transcript: An occasional prisoner or two committed by the houses of parliament. The courts of King's Bench. Common, please.

nova-3:68b8c9aa09607eca1402f5164996951fb.transcript: The exchequer, the commissioners of bankruptcy and of taxes, smugglers in a larger number sentence for very short terms.

nova-3:e8e4da0231ffbd4e1f91b7aefc29d9520.transcript: And for offenses of the most varying description by the Central Criminal Court.

nova-3:7becae3e31eebdd378cbc2415bdb64839.transcript: The sum total thus produced was inconsiderable compared with the hundreds that had formally filled the jail.

nova-3:c62a9ace8840ae3b736c65655bd36d4b2.transcript: And the hole by proper management might have been so accommodated as to prevent overcrowding.

nova-3:c27a276e084a4511dbd68ade4e414a2e2.transcript: But incredible as it may appear, the authorities of Newgate declined to avail themselves of the advantages offered them.

nova-3:bb72d61b34d2ef2cf2fccba62d62ee64a.transcript: And when the population fell, they shut up one half to jail and crowded up the other.

nova-3:5e05eb15ba84cb476975401e293ad15fa.transcript: Some rooms remained quite empty and unoccupied, while others were full to overflowing.

nova-3:122260a46457ee21a7b696fb8b72f5714.transcript: Not only were the wards thus needlessly crammed and for no reason but the niggardliness of the corporation, which refused a proper supply of bedding.

nova-3:53c75ef7d07b9e5205337e57952a32176.transcript: The felon and the misdemeanor, the sane and the insane, the old and young offender.

nova-3:f0c9e9fc461fb978598e86aa876df66c9.transcript: But the occupants of each were huddled together indiscriminately. The inspectors found in the same wards in the chapel yard the convicted and the untried.

nova-3:23499bb67847e024587028aadb37e47c3.transcript: And the greatest contempt shown for the law.

nova-3:384dfbed9d41f3affa4c7051732bdbc60.transcript: The classification prescribed by the jail act, which laid down that certain prisoners should not intermix, was openly neglected.

nova-3:71c20cc0ef3d8e40653e1ea6173da2f28.transcript: Another part, there were men charged with and convicted of unnatural offenses, shut up with lads of tender years.

nova-3:474d1586e133d89e8f3a2a16fde797e53.transcript: Minor offenders charged with small thefts or nonpayment of small sums were cheek by jowl with convicts sentenced to long terms of transportation.

nova-3:101c242597da8af4c3e43470616d70fe1.transcript: In the master's side yard, which had only one washing place, as many as 78 prisoners, frequently more.

nova-3:84379f3e903c5d818e2da0e0b11cd7f57.transcript: We're associated together. It's of every variety of age, habit, and delinquency without employment, oversight, or control.

nova-3:f645769d8fba7ac23c2be3b186491ab07.transcript: The middle yard, it was still worse.

nova-3:0b0037bff6f58f0b8cf9d58d8ebbde97f.transcript: Here, say the inspectors, are herded together the very worst class of prisoners. Certainly, a more wretched combination of human beings can hardly be imagined.

nova-3:69c39f5d630201b880711c250774b2387.transcript: We have reason to fear that poverty, ragged clothes, and an inability to pay the war dues elsewhere exacted for better accommodation.

nova-3:f093b6010c76c554dec7d5f513ebd48bf.transcript: Consign many of the more petty and unpracticed offenders to this place.

nova-3:ca0404f8b870cd0d279edcdafdd9834f0.transcript: Where they inevitably meet with further contamination from the society of the most abandoned and incorrigible inmates of the jail.

nova-3:74c77aaf71c532efb36ca7f8d4872a88c.transcript: No doubt the governor, for the time being, mister Cope, was in a great measure to blame for all this and for the want of proper classification.

nova-3:3e7b87eaa5e8452ac6da66f94ef219549.transcript: I shall have occasion to speak again and more at length of Mr. Cope's careless and perfunctory discharge.

nova-3:e69ec0d62f2c59da6bd627f86a0a0512d.transcript: Was unable to give any reason whatever for not utilizing the whole of the wards.

nova-3:2505a3a874dcdb1cdee33ea9030e19f17.transcript: Of his many manifest duties, but I shall here confine myself to animate verdict on his neglect as regards the appropriation of his prison.

nova-3:54dd8faf129bd35e6a0310cb7e8765c86.transcript: He saw certain rooms fill up and yet took no steps to open others that were locked up and empty.

nova-3:b227d479b7e4db34aee23a7d3c5f52d2c.transcript: He blamed the construction of Newgate for the neglect of classification and was yet compelled to confess that he had made no attempt whatever to carry it out.

nova-3:60d70323dbf249b4f8bf11154d2dce876.transcript: The fact was he did not keep the classification of prisoners on first arrival in his own hands nor even in that of his officers.

nova-3:b677bda3ab501f38a41ffccfbb6298f6d.transcript: A new prisoner's fate as to location rested really with a powerful fellow prisoner.

nova-3:e7c5c597f099c1805f08638113c24eaad.transcript: The inspectors found that prisoners had their places assigned to them.

nova-3:07481c4de6214d0c5cc1a992d56b0fb50.transcript: By the inner gatesman, himself a convicted prisoner and a wardsman or responsible head of a room.

nova-3:722dcc284b185836743a0a62087cfe707.transcript: The wardsman still exacted dues. What? Sheesh. Of which more directly?

nova-3:5c0fa0f0ca07936d0bcfa8e64d742e569.transcript: So great is the authority exercised by him.

nova-3:d9946273b43afc544b78e51f30127153e.transcript: And this particular official took excellent care to select his residents for his own ward, those most suitable from his own point of view.

nova-3:3894eaeb4969be6b7dff53e7e043bc846.transcript: And so numerous were his opportunities of showing favoritism that all the prisoners may be said to be in his power.

nova-3:0fad2fa82d68404242185168bcb3318e2.transcript: If a man is poor and ragged, however inexperienced in crime, or however trifling may be the offense for which he has been committed.

nova-3:ee08528ca3f9e55bf927662df8160c2ec.transcript: His place is assigned among the most depraved, the most experienced, and the most incorrigible offenders in the middle yard.

nova-3:b4bd5b78889b4790a5d1d36f29d81596a.transcript: Their treatment was also a matter of chance. They still slept on rope mats on the floor, herded together in companies of four or more to keep one another warm.

nova-3:6e86e507d659014062b7e23574a70492e.transcript: It was not likely that a system which left innocent men for the great bulk of new arrivals were still untried.

nova-3:91e4cdf8a174530e5c2cf19eeaf84bb04.transcript: So closely did they lie together that the inspectors at their night visits found it difficult in stepping across the room to avoid treading on them.

nova-3:793eb335ea27758fa9b940b7e34b6f8ac.transcript: To be pitchforked by chance anywhere into any sort of company.

nova-3:8df47ef24c4b372617714db1c02b2af36.transcript: Within this, the greatest nursery of crime in London should exercise even the commonest care for the personal decency or comfort of the prisoners.

nova-3:04f30814b966b26fc61d84e605e12ade2.transcript: Must be admitted that so far, but little effort had been made to counteract the evils of indiscriminate association.

nova-3:40c5ad88b9da09290acf6e5a49dffcbaa.transcript: And under the scanty covering of a couple of dirty stable rugs apiece.

nova-3:fd8f2fce0735663f231e3b0ec85d2fc24.transcript: Sometimes two mats were allotted to three sleepers. Sometimes four slept under the same bedding and left their mats unoccupied.

nova-3:7aa7deed9f9f9d97b3b667d4191281f8a.transcript: The rugs used were never washed. An order existed that the bedding should be taken into the yards to be aired, but it was not very punctually obeyed.

nova-3:c77cc850851a991a22fd99a9a1be07af4.transcript: The only convenience for personal ablutions were the pumps in the yards and the far off baths in the condemned or press yard.

nova-3:5349408c5e661e8cade6861fa5c882b7d.transcript: Water might not be taken into the ward for washing purposes.

nova-3:faf395aa39b3b9e9d630e0fa9f68355fa.transcript: The inspectors paraded the prisoners and found them generally ragged and ill clad, squalid and filthy in the extreme.

nova-3:a41cb2f1672b5d24009abca9c49990407.transcript: There was some provision of clothing, but it was quite insufficient, and nothing at all was given if prisoners had enough of their own to cover their nakedness.

nova-3:ff63c8d2f422e401921970510b5addeb8.transcript: Many without stockings and with hardly shoes to their feet.

nova-3:f34c8203b37b4dae54cad836cf32a84eb.transcript: Some who had the semblance of covering on the upper part of their feet had no soles to the shoes, and their bare feet were on the ground.

nova-3:9c9c59f6675290fc6756e8a50d3de079e.transcript: This too was in this depth of the winter and during a most inclement season.

nova-3:9cd92ffca072e684c3c4659a7f1450894.transcript: The allowance of food was not a liberal.

nova-3:2d78f1844bccd693ffb4b7b4f53a09860.transcript: But its issue was precarious and dependent on the goodwill of the wardsman who measured out the portions to each according to his eye.

nova-3:616b7efe6f4eb4c57217e0db3cdb68614.transcript: Not with weights and measures, no turnkey being present.

nova-3:01a888816ebf0072e351b6406f8328dc3.transcript: Too much was left to the wardsman. It was he who could issue small luxuries.

nova-3:831dcdf1d2e2100ed8321d066eaecab81.transcript: He sold tea, coffee, sugar, tobacco, although prohibited, and extra beer.

nova-3:b33d11ceffeaee209e899581ebc5f95ce.transcript: He charged a weekly sum as war dues for the use of knives, forks, and plates.

nova-3:1e2680128f0698782dde02740a3f430e6.transcript: A perpetuation under another form of the old detestable custom of garnish.

nova-3:b75ba24ad6d402060bf42636adbba7a9f.transcript: He had power where his exactions were resisted of making the ward most uncomfortable for the defaulter.

nova-3:35dc4386b8e9812374bd835eb3ad139bd.transcript: Could trump up a false complaint against his fellow prisoner and so get him punished.

nova-3:ffcebf2db0565562378ab574d4c7b3adc.transcript: Might keep him from the fire or give him his super gruel in a pail instead of a basin.

nova-3:58a72ec53cfd4296454a0ea7ce185f263.transcript: The authority of these wardsmen so improperly exalted and so entirely unchecked degenerated into a baneful despotism.

nova-3:fde6b0d775a65d5678c147d3e2b74ba22.transcript: They bought their offices from one another and were thus considered to have a vested interest in them.

nova-3:9d04508db5239f49a5d05848c8bd565ef.transcript: Their original capital had been a few shillings, and for this, they purchased the right to tax their fellows to the extent of pounds per week.

nova-3:9e8585cc72439da0dcf467395444ae801.transcript: The wardsman had a monopoly in supplying provisions, gave dinner and breakfast at his own price, and was such complete master of the ward.

nova-3:a3f479ba91ffb8a03e3b3109dc848bb9d.transcript: That none of its inmates were suffered to make tea or coffee for themselves, lest it should interfere with his sales.

nova-3:8101b4fda3fc1cd3d3732b887175a6513.transcript: Made collections when it suited him for award purposes to be spent as he chose in candles and so forth.

nova-3:b355ebebeb0c509e27cfdcd25f0ad4fd3.transcript: When the wardsman was a man of some education, with some knowledge of legal chicanery gained by personal experience, he might add considerably to his emoluments.

nova-3:3440ac94c494324af67e8a6d5da54c439.transcript: By drawing briefs and petitions for his fellows. There was a recognized charge of 5 shillings per brief.

nova-3:27ce73e82c81d52f1ff176b10c03af8b6.transcript: For a petition of from 1 shilling 0.5p to 8 shillings according to its length

nova-3:dd33f8faaf84a5018075b958bc19e1b84.transcript: And by these payments, awardsmen had been known to amass as much as £40.

nova-3:7c6cc98a788027edaeb2acaf609d60b85.transcript: The man entrusted with this privilege was often the inner gatesman.

nova-3:2ecd39030ada85a5747fc6a3c9639584b.transcript: The prisoner official already mentioned who held the fate of new arrivals as regards location in his hands.

nova-3:8c5389800efe3cc50c01753813d2ef496.transcript: Had been known to employ threats declaring that he was often consulted by the governor as to a prisoner's character.

nova-3:50755b575e883969471141c90379fffea.transcript: It was not strange that he should sometimes misuse his power. And when prisoners were not to be cajoled into securing his legal services

nova-3:1aa5222792d1da3a2b452cb03f5502379.transcript: In view of speaking to it at the trial, and he could easily do them a good turn or a very bad one.

nova-3:dd28185e614bc6c0c70673029088927df.transcript: The brief drawing gatesman and wardsman at the time of the inspector's first visit must have been a particularly powerful personage.

nova-3:4c7473c6e594e0908157b8114a31618d3.transcript: He was on the most intimate and improperly familiar terms with the turnkeys.

nova-3:82d712ea68e1df320dfa77c65229490be.transcript: Had a key of both the master side and middle side yards, was the only person present at the distribution of beer and was trusted to examine.

nova-3:341ab7070d6ddeeeb9a14afa3dac277d6.transcript: And if he chose, pass in all provisions, money, clothes, and letters brought for prisoners by their friends.

nova-3:c0989850365304c889d873014db765b2a.transcript: The wardsman alike were more or less irresponsible.

nova-3:62d704ea93634386668ce5b23ba6a2d35.transcript: The turnkeys complained bitterly that these old prisoners had more power than they themselves.

nova-3:8617560441032243d06f2784d7e5a2186.transcript: The governor himself admitted that a prisoner of weak intellect who had been severely beaten and much injured by a wardsman did not dare complain.

nova-3:86965af4845b40f69aa2f0308bf5a0b64.transcript: The victim of this cruel ill usage having more fear of the power of the wardsman to injure him than confidence in the governor's power to protect him.

nova-3:5163192fd827f31eb8b4396ea2ebf6a4a.transcript: These wardsmen, besides thus ruling the roast, had numerous special privileges. If such, they can be called.

nova-3:3fdc9d04b2e65d9c2645348df34309247.transcript: They were not obliged to attend chapel and seldom, if ever, went. Prisoners, said one of them under examination, did not like the trouble of going to chapel.

nova-3:83a6f1e2619561abc77cbf56294866cb7.transcript: They had a standing bedstead to sleep on and a good flock mattress. Double allowance of provisions, filched from the common stock.

nova-3:a8508c64ad727f31a948fc7eafe663289.transcript: Nobody interfered with them or regulated their conduct. They might get drunk when so disposed and did so frequently alone or in company.

nova-3:7cceddd965a5c6d16ca4bd2aad110a65c.transcript: Evidence was given before the inspectors of eight or 10 prisoners seen giddy drunk, not able to sit upon forms.

nova-3:9e8730e644fc62fc92ae3f97ab3b8aa8b.transcript: The female wards women were also given to intemperance.

nova-3:7777467ad12d886ab21087b0924ea921f.transcript: The matron deposed to having seen the gateswoman exceedingly drunk and having been insulted by her.

nova-3:0c2ebce02f7ff78f11a735615a288273e.transcript: There was no penalty attached to drunkenness.

nova-3:ef7bf771fae86a1a3346c4859e8adcee4.transcript: Awardsman did not necessarily lose his situation for it, nor was drink the only creature comfort he might enjoy.

nova-3:239cbb92e9e78b4bd1364e609fb82b1f4.transcript: He could indulge in snuff if a snuff taker.

nova-3:b2fc7b7c9d33baf0690e81114ac0f45ea.transcript: Was still freely introduced into the prison.

nova-3:4e84bbbb6ba4a5b253b5aaba04b759858.transcript: And might always smoke his pipe undisturbed. For although the use of tobacco had been prohibited since the report of the Lord's Committee

nova-3:c7edb63572d12d9ca28de8c39b8028fa6.transcript: Probably authority would not have been so recklessly usurped by the wardsman had not the proper officials too readily surrendered it.

nova-3:9793512faae9c4c48a3589d399a8614de.transcript: The turnkeys left the prisoners very much to themselves, never entering the wards after locking up time at dusk till unlocking next morning.

nova-3:493573f20e6adb61e0a94c4edd9b4984e.transcript: And then only went round to count the number.

nova-3:faba4c427595bfcb32c04f90dfb1f3ac7.transcript: One turnkey had been so employed several hours daily for nearly eleven years.

nova-3:fb55324ebc929bcec44933efb8cd384d4.transcript: Many of them were otherwise and improperly occupied for hours every day in menial services for the governor, cleaning his windows or grooming his horse.

nova-3:e22fc644a72d65f0b9bea0b38949c2d6a.transcript: It was not strange that subordinates should neglect their duty when superior set the example.

nova-3:118648ce342311d46e7aa37315da4c778.transcript: Nothing was more prominently brought out by the inspectors than the inefficiency of the governor at that time, mister Cope.

nova-3:2b7c9fdbb81a8b9287aee80667faf908f.transcript: We have seen that he took no pains to classify and separate prisoners on reception.

nova-3:e32ea26e0864997fc77c9339310ab1ef2.transcript: May have erred in some points through ignorance, but in others, he was clearly guilty of culpable neglect.

nova-3:b4c755984a00d5b72dd0eb86845f823da.transcript: This was only one of many grave omissions on his part. He did not feel it incumbent on himself to visit his prison often or see his prisoners.

nova-3:5a3b0e0edf6eb7abb46d89e888f3f7011.transcript: The act prescribed that he should do both every twenty four hours, but days passed without his entering the wards.

nova-3:a1d4617794f7ca86e29dddd6b1c23a9e4.transcript: One man who had been in the condemned ward for two months said the governor only came there four times.

nova-3:2d07ef627286a9385262789e224945060.transcript: The prisoners declared that they did not see him oftener than twice a week.

nova-3:b5e0ce037d7825a966d16d5a604e22ce6.transcript: Again, a turnkey deposed that his chief did not enter the wards more than once a fortnight.

nova-3:e94c2bd15f5108814b5998de899ee4215.transcript: But it is only fair to mister Cope to state that he himself said he went whenever he could find time.

nova-3:8cbd7480776bb3a4169a1fcd807f7945d.transcript: And that he was constantly engaged attending sessions and going with drafts to the Hawks.

nova-3:5b1650b5c2ec7a5aa1562ad0fa252448c.transcript: But when he did visit, his inspections were of the most superficial character.

nova-3:7bdb5cc029dc2220a27d4d2c7133ed287.transcript: Dice dangerous implements or other prohibited articles.

nova-3:3824d73c07aa041f990ae2b7c8276e758.transcript: Sometimes he looked at his bolts and bars, but he never examined the cupboards, coal boxes, or other possible hiding places for cards.

nova-3:f0bf7c5c406c4a4a3862b2ed055a0a392.transcript: To taking the descriptions of newly arrived prisoners.

nova-3:54b0270b3bffe6fda0500a771f4e09354.transcript: Only attended chapel once on Sunday, never on the weekday, and generally devoted the time service was in progress.

nova-3:d4411cacdb249f64aa7385cc94fda6034.transcript: Really did not know what passed in his jail.

nova-3:5fb7ef91f8d9b197b9b5cea15e698e7d2.transcript: And was surprised when the inspectors proved to him that practices of which he was ignorant and which he admitted that he reprehended went on without hindrance.

nova-3:ce9d3ca832b34420de6f3dfa351d3ca13.transcript: He was satisfied to let matters run on as in the old times, he said in his own justification. With him, what was was right.

nova-3:d65251c76299095ee875947f748fca0ba.transcript: And evils that should have been speedily rooted out remained because they had the prescription of long usage.

nova-3:7fccd59f31b72948030a6923d231fc875.transcript: He kept no daily journal of occurrences, and nothing, however important, was recorded at the time.

nova-3:0d479bcbb72bd29017b0ab723d778fd95.transcript: The alderman never called upon him to report and left him nearly unsupervised and uncontrolled.

nova-3:f964478707a89e01a78fa66597f63651e.transcript: His administration of discipline, he was quite uncertain.

nova-3:40b1bf270e0f9ba6e28153dc546f2a564.transcript: And it was not the least part of the blame imputed to him that he made special favorites of particular prisoners, retaining of his own accord in Newgate.

nova-3:f4de71472c7a631fe531a1978019e703a.transcript: And for years, felons who should have been sent beyond the seas.

nova-3:5945bc7ba777e4edba797e9e59780bafc.transcript: But indeed his whole rule was far too mild. And under this mistaken leniency

nova-3:d5578e620233cc2561459bae49239d87e.transcript: The interior of the jail was more like a bear garden or the noisy perlues of a public house than a prison.

nova-3:4a41ffd7666c9bc3afd70c0acfa846e2b.transcript: Under the reckless contempt for regulations

nova-3:e4292391a862d943db454bfcbf56016a2.transcript: It was the same old story, evil constantly in the ascendant, the least criminal at the mercy of the most depraved.

nova-3:31f4ef18a5e93865be6335ab3c408f721.transcript: The apathy of the authorities and the undue ascendancy of those who, as convicted felons, should have been most sternly repressed.

nova-3:29864f9236eb1abb3599556884f621d04.transcript: The most hardened and the oldest in vice had the best of it, while the inexperienced beginner went to the wall.

nova-3:d204cb564065533fc4e0dbe9168569609.transcript: Said with Justice that incredible scenes of horror occur in Newgate.

nova-3:a50a9cab51b58bc14a72e8b31d83c8411.transcript: Edward Gibbon Wakefield, who spent three years in Newgate a little before the time of the inspector's first report

nova-3:1e3fe326859fda6bd88b759353eac0570.transcript: It was, moreover, in his opinion, undoubtedly the greatest nursery of crime in London.

nova-3:96fbb5d64acb7c7189bd7f5b01b0eb87d.transcript: A second room were 14 more who had every hope of a reprieve.

nova-3:b0db09a7b38f721277e2de813ec8bc723.transcript: The whole of these 17 had, however, a common airing yard and took their exercise there at the same time.

nova-3:123a69d05f3f66fd930a808d0d590e2d7.transcript: So that men in the most awful situation, daily expecting to be hanged

nova-3:8d89f93f156d1902deb628f805062210c.transcript: Were associated continually with a number of those who could look with certainty on a mitigation of punishment.

nova-3:99510c786752851f895f326130e7e80bd.transcript: The latter, lighthearted and reckless, conducted themselves in the most unseemly fashion and with as much indifference as the inmates of the other parts of the prison.

nova-3:6ba383519993bebb88e55425b3588dec9.transcript: They amused themselves after their own fashion. Played all day long at blind man's buff and leapfrog or beat each other with a knotted handkerchief.

nova-3:008c1b562709d66976db52886929c0cee.transcript: Men whose cases were dangerous and those most seriously inclined complained of these annoyances.

nova-3:83617c0f9ffb6faee13654f7158d3ee21.transcript: Laughing and uproarious, utterly unmindful of the companionship of men upon whom lay the shadow of an impending shameful death.

nova-3:e16810d42f6d32205d7a3b4e89fa023c4.transcript: So subversive of meditation, so disturbing to the thoughts.

nova-3:2124d94feab166f569cd98f2e617ec133.transcript: They suffered sickening anxiety and wished to be locked up alone. This indiscriminate association lasted for months.

nova-3:5977c35e7cd3b50358495c92438b4b9c1.transcript: During the whole of which time the unhappy convicts who had but little hope of commutation were exposed to the mockery of their reckless associates.

nova-3:92dbb8f818a2cd536151c8c5d72f951af.transcript: The brutal callousness of the bulk of the inmates of the press yard may be gathered from the prison punishment book, which frequently recorded such entries as the following.

nova-3:d659a413e7ada2d8e456037aa46c579ae.transcript: Benjamin Vines and Daniel Ward put in irons for two days for breaking the windows of the day room in the condemned cells.

nova-3:07cc5c59ee367f4b1601778b8e0c063d9.transcript: Joseph Coleman put in irons for three days for striking one of the prisoners in the same place.

nova-3:d5d700df5479f40e5f48ee03d7bfd4c55.transcript: The more peaceably disposed found some occupation in making Newgate tokens.

nova-3:fbc9949be70ee45003596b71794ee124c.transcript: There were disputes and quarrels constantly among these doomed men. It was a word and blow, an argument clenched always with a fight.

nova-3:d15d2a34228e1314291a288388495bf84.transcript: Turnkeys occasionally visited the press yard, but its occupants were under little or no control.

nova-3:2067cc8687262877e5b0ee8fe8adc437f.transcript: Leaden hearts and grinding the impressions off penny pieces, then pricking figures or words on them to give to their friends as memorials.

nova-3:2587c1f8dc3cebc042f458c342faeb8dc.transcript: Had relaxed his efforts because according to his own account, he was so frequently stopped in the performance of his duties.

nova-3:dd3a845a87fe22fd1ba78c1f8f4715302.transcript: The chaplain who might have been expected to make these men his peculiar care and who at one time had visited them frequently, often several times a week

nova-3:d654a3b789a046dde85b82462c24b65f0.transcript: In his evidence before the inspectors, he declared that for years, he gave his whole time to his duties from an early hour in the morning to late in the afternoon.

nova-3:3877b135edf18246f2c9ac6e9a87b1f1c.transcript: He left off because he was so much interfered with and laughed at and from seeing that no success attended his efforts owing to the evils arising from association.

nova-3:97e53df3323db070062fcc165f7d29deb.transcript: Latterly, administrations to the condemned had been restricted to a visit on Sunday afternoons and occasionally about once a fortnight on a weekday.

nova-3:06ffffa5b15f26a5dc647d2c113ed7089.transcript: It is only fair to mister Cotton to add that, according to his own journal, he was unremitting in his attentions to convicts who were actually cast for death.

nova-3:b8c2e6c59fb5d0d1b44db57380930d590.transcript: And the day of whose execution was fixed. He had no doubt a difficult mission to discharge.

nova-3:6b891a7f58877d35f4e6bc4bf871092c5.transcript: On the one hand, the ladies association, supported and encouraged by public approval, trenched upon his peculiar province.

nova-3:19a85ddcfc615144c0369c179a232edb8.transcript: On the other, the governor of the jail sneered at his zeal.

nova-3:eb9d1269f0ada800ca9d96e0fff815b91.transcript: Stigmatized his often most just strictures on abuses as a bundle of nonsense. And the aldermen, when he appealed to them for protection and countenance

nova-3:2afc1890efb6ee081424989336c24d9c2.transcript: Generally sided with his opponents. Nevertheless, the inspectors summed up against him.

nova-3:09c2f07511c47f63e050a3b6397a6292f.transcript: While admitting that he had had many difficulties to contend with

nova-3:b235686c10dbd98e949f54b86f1b52764.transcript: And that he had again and again protested against the obstacles thrown in his way. The inspectors cannot forbear expressing their opinion that he might have shown greater perseverance.

nova-3:737e45fc24e2dc95df899db0b881cb4ba.transcript: In the face of impediments, confessedly discouraging.

nova-3:28a9c7c6a1c3abe274cefaaf8cbc284fa.transcript: To that line of conduct which his duty imposed on him.

nova-3:5e7a0d67513fe1f70d792ea56c585aa26.transcript: As regards the private teaching of prisoners. And they went on to say that a resolved adherence in spite of discouragement is the most disheartening.

nova-3:dd3096c3e4b675976b3a31f2a44869867.transcript: Would, it is probable, have eventually overcome the reluctance of some of the prisoners at least and would have possessed so much moral dignity.

nova-3:7ae11b17e2a9a5fb853d41af3b5fddf13.transcript: As effectually to rebuke and abash the profane spirit of the more insolent and daring of the criminals.

nova-3:75c4003e6a819bc730489ea55ab5f95af.transcript: The lax discipline maintained in Newgate was still further deteriorated by the presence of two other classes of prisoners who ought never to have been inmates of such a jail.

nova-3:3efb439c4a0a35ebdb5a97df04c17b3df.transcript: One of these were the criminal lunatics who were at this time and for long previous continuously imprisoned there.

nova-3:03c9ce01ebaaf9c289a7bb983f05cf8aa.transcript: Or arraignment to an asylum, and the secretary of state had the same powers regards any who became insane while undergoing sentence.

nova-3:062d11a59b2e80bfd99699279fca6ed64.transcript: Has the law stood since the passing of the ninth? George the fourth c 40, any two justices might remove a prisoner found to be insane, either on commitment.

nova-3:11dfbc7397c4b2a21dac212dc25559a71.transcript: Whose proper place was the asylum?

nova-3:77449461d79d3904cb204dcbad5886949.transcript: These powers were not invariably put in force, and there were, in consequence, many unhappy lunatics in Newgate and other jails.

nova-3:16a731221e239c1202ca0df933023cd3e.transcript: At the time the Lord's committee sat, there were eight thus retained in Newgate. And a return in the appendix of the Lord's report

nova-3:c3ffefdbae3d6e836a5e967e3878040dc.transcript: Gives a total of 39 lunatics confined in various jails, many of them guilty of murder and other serious crimes.

nova-3:f253eac4b87828b21789563ba932245fd.transcript: The inspectors in the following year, on examining the facts, found that some of these poor creatures had been in confinement for long periods.

nova-3:316d617ed1946ab1d8b435a8ab5feeb4a.transcript: At Newgate and York Castle as long as five years, at Ilchester and Moorpith for seven years, at Warwick for eight years.

nova-3:b65cde481925943ddaa294eb0f221b39e.transcript: At Buckingham and Hereford for eleven years.

nova-3:34b1b9bd00f77fcde6ef11a9d65033ef7.transcript: At Appleby for thirteen years, at Anglesey for fifteen years, at Exeter for sixteen years, and at Pembroke.

nova-3:62317230ca53edd0402f75d0c85a2addd.transcript: Not less a period than twenty four year.

nova-3:282ab2a69a927713020d5fa7caba62fc0.transcript: It was manifestly wrong that such persons visited by the most awful of calamities should be detained in a common prison.

nova-3:3b4602188471b47accce27ab7982bfd85.transcript: Not only did their presence tend greatly to interfere with the discipline of the prison, but their condition was deplorable in the extreme.

nova-3:d1219c8e3fe6aa9d6f5d44a10f6c82f94.transcript: The lunatic became the sport of the idol and the depraved. His cure was out of the question.

nova-3:9dd0d39251d03b456c483ed1fa122e987.transcript: Was placed in a situation beyond all others calculated to confirm his malady and prolong his sufferings.

nova-3:0fee5395eb39f8194515cc3bd3cfc6a80.transcript: The matter was still further complicated at Newgate by the presence within the walls of sham lunatics. Some of those included in the category

nova-3:bf98d244b24c941757be3e9e5999f193a.transcript: Had actually been returned as sane from the asylum to which they had been sent, and there was always some uncertainty as to who was mad and who not.

nova-3:f7772b3f716ffacd689ef3d431bae9d4e.transcript: Prisoners indeed were known to boast that they had saved their necks by feigning insanity.

nova-3:eb4e8f9e8647a270062e8d6c4320df78a.transcript: It was high time that the unsatisfactory state of the law as regards the treatment of criminal lunatics should be remedied.

nova-3:3e9848add9fcd641aeae1a5dc60a4f6ca.transcript: And not the least of the good services rendered by the new inspectors was their inquiry into the status of these unfortunate people and their recommendation to improve it.

nova-3:0f0c437c9f66b8f33513333dd122908c5.transcript: The other inmates of the prison have an exceptional character and exempted from the regular disciplines such as it was.

nova-3:d6661af6d5f73d375a9aad0ff25ffb3cb.transcript: Were the 10 persons committed to Newgate by the House of Commons in 1835?

nova-3:2741897a34371d8921170f0ed4233dc45.transcript: These were the gentlemen concerned in the bribery case at Ipswich in 1835.

nova-3:35501f338a4053535b64111ae808c944b.transcript: When a petition was presented against the return of messers Adam Dundas and Fitzroy Kelly, various witnesses, including messers JB Desent

nova-3:3114dbef9dc31e35981f230ba1d0853f2.transcript: Pilgrim Bond and Clamp had refused to give evidence before the House of Commons Committee. A speaker's warrant was issued for their arrest when they absconded.

nova-3:c3634950c6f998f16d3b3d7822bf43123.transcript: Mr. J. E. Sparrow and Mr. Clipperton.

nova-3:59a5688c734c4c379786c5b5360d8e6fd.transcript: The parliamentary agents of the members whose election was impugned were implicated in aiding and abetting the others to abscond and a mister O'Malley

nova-3:646675f8da13a0966e51ff578d85f38de.transcript: Pilgrim and Descent were caught and given into the custody of the sergeant at arms, and the rest were either arrested or they surrendered.

nova-3:146ed1712236d68f38738e560e8fcac2a.transcript: A resolution at once passed the house without division to commit the whole to Newgate, where they remained for various terms.

nova-3:82ce117f42aa9c8ab70cc31b751c40cdc.transcript: Dazen and Pilgrim were released in ten days on making due submission.

nova-3:f46e28d70de2c950b71b87a89edc1c9ea.transcript: O'Malley sent in a medical certificate declaring that the imprisonment was endangering his life. And after some question, he was also released.

nova-3:fc4fe553fe2afa850bccf2748d5dc59e7.transcript: The rest were detained for more than a month. It being considered that they were the most guilty as being either professional agents who advised the others to abscond

nova-3:b4bb9a02707c0f38affa9657b44336e32.transcript: Or witnesses who did not voluntarily come forward when the chance was given them.

nova-3:952e792c550deb139a6aeb8eacdd14af5.transcript: Many of the old customs once prevalent in the stateside so properly condemned and abolished

nova-3:b0e6f631a29fc06c6f50a88d8190e865a.transcript: Were revived for the convenience of these gentlemen whose incarceration was thus rendered as little like imprisonment as possible.

nova-3:96dd1a4e0f359d07604483184c5802493.transcript: Certain number who could afford the high rate of a guinea per diem fixed by the undersheriff were lodged in the governor's House.

nova-3:72c3e24a750151ba988c44a2cf3779645.transcript: Slept there and had their meals provided for them from the Sessions House or London Coffee House.

nova-3:6292e40838a705c400f5fafb48e2104ef.transcript: A few others who could not afford a payment of more than 0.5 a guinea were permitted to monopolize a part of the prison infirmary.

nova-3:3f0e6f44e3ac5ee2d90a524f01cb79f5a.transcript: Where the upper ward was exclusively appropriated to their use. They also had their meals sent in, and with the food, wine almost ad libetum.

nova-3:55679939ac1239ca79b2b2ac783251a12.transcript: A prisoner, one of the wardsman, waited on those in the infirmary. The occupants of the governor's house had their own servants or the governor's.

nova-3:308ea6af9033852c5630c5e8626740ebe.transcript: As a rule, visitors, many of them many of them persons of good position, came and went all day long and as late as nine at night.

nova-3:a7fb1fc05aa9eb85bc4af840c94facd02.transcript: Some to the infirmary, many more to the Governor's House.

nova-3:5e00d9a93f73f0632955161d229b6db28.transcript: There were no restraints, cards, backgammon were played, and the time passed in feasting and revelry.

nova-3:456b33cabe4f3b1471f1195e0502cddb2.transcript: Even mister Cope admitted that the committal of this class of prisoners to Newgate was most inconvenient.

nova-3:e415f726ee1b850c95829018edcf10285.transcript: And the inspectors expressed themselves still more strongly in reprehension of the practice.

nova-3:84b617a95466a937072ce8d7112d2d9f3.transcript: The infirmary at this particular period epitomized the condition of the jail at large.

nova-3:7ffcb4a09400ffbf4d9208e580ca4cb81.transcript: All the evils of indiscriminate association were strongly accentuated by the crowd collected within its narrow limits.

nova-3:4f09c52d7c7f2b4cfb4d5b1ecb4ace67d.transcript: Was diverted from its proper uses and as the place of the greatest comfort was allotted to persons who should not have been sent to Newgate at all.

nova-3:c7b6d4eefa8b0317411319a1b29802ad9.transcript: It may easily be imagined, say the inspectors, and speaking of the prison generally

nova-3:c3299bd9ef4e2a82927ffb58a7adc1d96.transcript: What must be the state of discipline in a place filled with characters so various as were assembled there? Where the tried and the untried, the sick and the healthy.

nova-3:964a2e3c65d0df64b2ac1a5405b63e3ae.transcript: The sane and the insane, the young and the old, the trivial offender, and the man about to suffer the extreme penalty of the law.

nova-3:4abf684aebbb8c208f5bf7fe0ce5146d9.transcript: All huddled together without discrimination, oversight, or control.

nova-3:72bca7452a30cf39863b81a49b14834c0.transcript: Enough has probably been extracted from this most damnatory report to give a complete picture of the disgraceful state in which Newgate still remained in 1835.

nova-3:548ebce4700da41a55088e5008c2fd313.transcript: The inspectors, however, honestly admitted that although the site of the prison was convenient, its construction was as bad as bad could be.

nova-3:b0e5954d6d3e78954dfffcdeb10de6db3.transcript: The wards were in some cases spacious, but they were entirely unsuited for separation or the inspection of prisoners.

nova-3:1d044e9b6b0e2e3b0204102076a797be3.transcript: Valuable space was cumbered with many long and winding passages, numerous staircases, and unnecessarily thick, encumbrance inner walls.

nova-3:40f52eb5badf392c8953f5feb38499dc9.transcript: But there are others remediable under a better system of management.

nova-3:947ef6b58455022b65accf71a173dff20.transcript: The yards were narrow and confined mainly because the ground plan was radically vicious. These were evils inseparable from the place.

nova-3:83a14c3a1a259a8daabfbfb77e20e8d62.transcript: Who constantly breathed in air heavy, and when the wards were first opened in the morning, particularly offensive.

nova-3:891393e44b560d91d15986d7ccda0f624.transcript: More attention to ventilation, which was altogether neglected and inadequate, would have secured a better atmosphere for the unhappy inmates.

nova-3:dc285c2fd6123b71061ce0b98afdd14f2.transcript: Again, the discipline commonly deemed inseparable from every place of endurance was entirely wanting.

nova-3:53bc3cd9f320a5672a6a7b5d0dc916858.transcript: The primary object of committing a prisoner to jail, as the inspectors pointed out, was to deter not only the criminal himself but others from crime.

nova-3:71cdc2dc46ae0072540b4047d17610d09.transcript: And to dispose him by meditation and seclusion to return to an honest life.

nova-3:2ba3b4a9478d1d762794221b9bd729edc.transcript: But at Newgate, the convicted prisoner, instead of privation and hard fare

nova-3:e2e60fe4cd0837f55f824acaf7c3866c6.transcript: Is permitted to purchase whatever his own means or the means of his friends in or out of prison can afford.

nova-3:e6f3f374452b6ff6cfdcb3b86b67e42b8.transcript: And he can almost invariably procure the luxuries of his class of life, beer and tobacco, in abundance.

nova-3:ab8b5ac6d96cce73eb82c3a1d423cb1ef.transcript: Vaunting his own adventures or listening to those of others.

nova-3:1d450e8911c3c7bb04fbc94177de3cab8.transcript: Instead of seclusion and meditation, his time has passed in the midst of a body of criminals of every class and degree, in riot debauchery, and gaming.

nova-3:09fbba26a96dcde6ce6305d5e53347c51.transcript: Communicating his own skill and aptitude in crime or acquiring the lessons of greater adepts. He has access to newspapers and, of course

nova-3:4fa45c632e5c9f05acc9552752e44aadc.transcript: Prefers that description which are expressly prepared for his own class and which abound in vulgar adventure and criminal enterprise and in the histories of the police.

nova-3:9689a6427e1e326fd9fdc0cccd83bfa5b.transcript: He's allowed intercourse with prostitutes who, in nine cases out of 10, have originally conduced to his ruin.

nova-3:536e1ac2f134e4ae1d7d0be1a65019d65.transcript: And his connection with them is confirmed by that devotion and generosity towards their paramours in adversity for which these otherwise degraded women are remarkable.

nova-3:2c4cd3626a35295fe4c9316c06c2baf69.transcript: Having thus passed his time, he returns a greater adept in crime with a wider acquaintance among criminals and what perhaps is even more injurious to him.

nova-3:c6b8999b0da1a74828197ff568ac64d2f.transcript: Is generally known to all the worst men in the country, not only without the inclination, but almost without the ability of returning to an honest life.

nova-3:ca4fc77d5a4dcb2cf9efbb1f9458a7938.transcript: These pungent and well grounded strictures applied with still greater force to the unconvicted prisoner, the man who came to the prison innocent and still uncontaminated.

nova-3:6ace315adff7abe389cf7bf8339b1e675.transcript: To be subjected to the same painful influences and to suffer the same moral deterioration, whether ultimately convicted or set free.

nova-3:dc6e1a68953631f52aa04ac97ed18d3a7.transcript: The whole system, or more correctly, the want of system, was painful and pernicious to the last degree.

nova-3:a34e9f2f57ff946636b40dc5a62aee485.transcript: The evils of such association were aggravated by the unbroken idleness. One evil inflamed the other, reformation.

nova-3:d2316bea6e9fa99def56db32c85964901.transcript: Any kind of moral improvement was impossible. The prisoner's career was inevitably downward till he struck the lowest depths.

nova-3:9440639e2e88be04d172d459f311df010.transcript: Forced in constant intercourse with the most depraved individuals of his own class.

nova-3:0c2443d9e47498a3ad1fde68609a54f81.transcript: The employment of those means and agents by which the lowest passions and the most vulgar propensities of man are perpetually kept in the highest state of excitement.

nova-3:32c2eafa86cdda93c93ac64cde94af6d8.transcript: Drink, gaming, obscene and blasphemous language, utter idleness, the almost unrestricted admission of money and luxuries.

nova-3:6b61d58a25f47abeaf552f62526a146bd.transcript: All the tumultuous and diversified passions and emotions which circumstances like these must necessarily generate.

nova-3:0b30cc21dbcd1a126ffde85888ae9e66a.transcript: Uncontrolled conversation with visitors of the very worst description, prostitutes, thieves, receivers of stolen goods.

nova-3:6f9f03e475041bfc9d2c30ad208f2c5c4.transcript: Forbid the faintest shadow of a hope that in a soil so unfavorable for moral culture.

nova-3:24d6ebf78ee38b3dfff5ce7a7c05764a9.transcript: Any awakening truth, salutary exhortation, or imperfect resolutions of amendment can take root or grow.

nova-3:057c5a14b069ae82e77e2f626a4e180a9.transcript: Strong as were the foregoing remarks, the inspectors wound up their report in still more trenchant language.

nova-3:b71991b668adbecd4c4ec15c800250a61.transcript: Framing a terrible indictment against those responsible for the condition of Newgate. Their words deserve to be quoted in full.

nova-3:600f3f372de6c3994ac30a09e1b615612.transcript: We cannot close these remarks, say the inspectors, without an expression of the painful feelings with which we submit to your lordship.

nova-3:f8cec0ad7a4996887cb9fbbeafb1b04d1.transcript: This picture of the existing state of Newgate.

nova-3:bc09b8b884843d36f1948289e8a57b651.transcript: That in this vast metropolis, the center of wealth, civilization, and information

nova-3:02ffca624395ad6c30cb727b512bab422.transcript: Distinguished as the seat of religion, worth, and philanthropy.

nova-3:7bac1d4727adb02d998d508b3b1ce75ba.transcript: Where is to be found in operation every expedient by which ignorance may be superseded by knowledge, idleness by industry, and suffering by benevolence.

nova-3:995dc41302df65a7146a285af328987d3.transcript: That in the metropolis of this highly favored country to which the eyes of other lands turn, for example, a system of prison discipline such as that enforced in Newgate.

nova-3:9643a7d100d3b62301e1237e35c66bb79.transcript: But in opposition to the recorded denunciations of authority and in defiance of the express enactments of the law

nova-3:99f6f7bc06ff82ce96b5aa77c2e27f149.transcript: Should be for a number of years in undisturbed operation, not only in contempt of religion and humanity.

nova-3:5bfdf85873806e84cf269f88d6561ac4d.transcript: We trust, however, that the day is at hand when this stain will be removed from the character of the city of London.

nova-3:dac3fa1e4127b174b9eba6237f2cfac1f.transcript: Is indeed a subject which cannot but impress every considerate mind with humiliation and sorrow.

nova-3:9c9942e42fe7086fe355f3749a3547356.transcript: Defeats the ends of justice, and disgraces the profession of a Christian country.

nova-3:a90f6dd968d75d457e688e3514f182098.transcript: And when the first municipal authority of our land will be no longer subjected to the reproach of fostering an institution which outrages the rights and feelings of humanity.

nova-3:bf5e825ae6c940563e65ae70eb777bf0c.transcript: The publication of this report raised a storm in the city, and the corporation was roused to make an immediate protest.

nova-3:5a7b8f559fe81f33bb92f6c89b421bec5.transcript: A committee of aldermen was forthwith appointed to report upon the inspector's report.

nova-3:1b0f6398bc01051066d4d2c69e66d59e2.transcript: And the result was another lengthy blue book printed in the parliamentary papers, 1836.

nova-3:118381158fb695bc79c4167906c04d008.transcript: Traversing where it was possible the statements of the inspectors and offering explanation and palliation of such evils as could not be denied.

nova-3:19f0df03ab4eec35ea72d503219e5eef1.transcript: The inspectors retorted without loss of time, reiterating their charges and pointing out that the committee of aldermen by its own admission

nova-3:1fba232148a3b6236f8e0145e63c6edb0.transcript: The undue authority given to prisoners, the levying of garnish under another name

nova-3:0c6ffb0be85b293732d7e38d4023a6492.transcript: Justified the original allegations. It was impossible to deny the indiscriminate association, the gambling, drinking, smoking, quarreling in the jail.

nova-3:492d1be6da67a4efee9d23bbab18a9716.transcript: The misemployment of officers and prisoners by the governor.
